title.narrative: Output 3.5. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement labour market programmes and employment services for transitions to decent work over the life course, with particular focus on young and older workers

description.narrative:
The Employment Agency of Montenegro (EAM) adopted a new organizational structure and procedures as the first stage of a comprehensive multi-year reform that is instrumental to Montenegro's European Union accession process.
Protocols for profiling persons not in employment neither in education or training (NEETs), methods to refine targeting were adopted and an activation programme was designed. Institutional strengthening set the ground for the establishment of a Youth Guarantee in the country. With resources made available by the Good Governance Fund (GGF), a unit of the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth, Development Office, the ILO prepared a review of the internal procedures of the Employment Agency of Montenegro that led to recommendations for the revision of the internal and external procedures, also in response to the COVID-19 crisis by including basic steps toward digitalization.
The ILO provided support in profiling persons NEETs and in methods to refine targeting and design an activation programme.
The work with the ministry and the public employment service on preparing the ground for the youth guarantee relied significantly on the ILO's facilitation of peer-learning and South-South and triangular cooperation (SSTC) with other public employment services.
